Proficiency in cloud AI/ML platforms and services such as Amazon Bedrock, AWS SageMaker, Azure AI Foundry, Azure Machine Learning, Google Vertex AI, and related model hosting, retrieval, agent, and evaluation capabilities.
Experience with enterprise data and AI ecosystems such as Databricks, Snowflake, Spark, Kafka, dbt, vector databases, lakehouse architectures, and modern data governance patterns.

jobs.title: AI/ML Engineer
jobs.description:
About BackOps

BackOps is building the AI resolution layer for companies that make or move physical goods.

The physical economy still runs on a fragmented web of ERPs, WMSs, TMSs, carrier and vendor portals, email, spreadsheets, legacy systems, and the people who know how to hold all of it together. When something breaks, whether a shipment is delayed, an order changes, a claim needs to be filed, a document is missing, someone has to gather context across systems, determine what should happen next, take action, and make sure the problem is actually resolved.

BackOps automates that work.

Our platform, Relay, deploys AI operators that understand operational workflows, work across the systems our customers already use, take action, navigate exceptions, and carry work through to resolution. We aren't building another dashboard or copilot. We're building the execution layer that sits between systems and gets the work done.

We recently raised a $42M Series B led by Insight Partners, just six months after our Series A, and are scaling across some of the largest companies in logistics, manufacturing, retail, and other industries that power the physical world.

The opportunity ahead is much larger than any single workflow or vertical. We're building the infrastructure for AI to operate reliably inside the real world.

The Role

As an AI/ML Engineer, you'll own the infrastructure and systems that make Relay's underlying intelligence more capable, efficient, and reliable.

Building an AI operator that can reason through a workflow is one challenge. Making that intelligence perform consistently across thousands of real-world operational scenarios, fragmented enterprise systems, and unpredictable conditions is another.

That's the problem you'll help solve.

You'll work at the intersection of machine learning, distributed systems, and production AI, designing the infrastructure that supports model execution, inference optimization, evaluation, and continuous improvement. You'll help determine how we select, adapt, deploy, and optimize the models powering Relay, balancing intelligence and quality with the performance, scalability, and economics required for enterprise production.

This isn't a role focused on integrating AI APIs or maintaining an established ML stack. You'll make foundational technical decisions, build capabilities from the ground up, and work closely with our CTO and engineering teams to advance the intelligence behind our products.

This is a senior individual contributor role with extraordinary leverage. You'll help define the AI/ML foundation BackOps scales on.

What You'll Own

Build the infrastructure behind Relay's intelligence

Own the architecture and engineering of the AI/ML systems that power Relay, enabling our models to run reliably, efficiently, and at scale.

That may include:

Model serving, inference pipelines, and execution infrastructure
Model selection, routing, and orchestration
Shared interfaces for accessing foundation models and specialized ML capabilities
Infrastructure for experimentation, evaluation, and production deployment
Model versioning, configuration, and lifecycle management
Compute orchestration and resource optimization where appropriate

You'll make pragmatic decisions about what we build, what we leverage from existing providers, and where custom infrastructure creates a meaningful advantage.

Make intelligence faster, more efficient, and more scalable

Our agents need to do more than produce the right answer. They need to operate within the performance and reliability constraints of real enterprise workflows.

You'll optimize the infrastructure and execution patterns that determine how efficiently our models perform, including latency, throughput, scalability, and inference cost.

You'll identify bottlenecks across the AI/ML stack, evaluate architectural tradeoffs, and implement improvements that allow us to support increasingly sophisticated workloads without sacrificing quality or reliability.

The goal isn't simply to make models run faster. It's to make better intelligence economically viable at scale.

Continuously improve model intelligence and quality

Model capability is evolving rapidly. Our ability to translate those advances into better outcomes for customers needs to evolve just as quickly.

You'll develop the systems and technical approaches that allow us to systematically improve model quality and effectiveness.

That may include:

Model evaluation, benchmarking, and comparative testing
Model selection and routing based on task complexity and performance
Context engineering, retrieval, and other techniques that improve model effectiveness
Fine-tuning, model adaptation, or specialized ML approaches where warranted
Experimentation frameworks that connect model changes to measurable improvements in production

You'll partner closely with engineers building Relay's agent capabilities to understand where model limitations create execution failures and determine the most effective way to address them.

Engineer reliability into production AI

AI systems are probabilistic. Enterprise operations demand consistency, accountability, and predictable behavior.

You'll build the infrastructure required to operate AI/ML workloads reliably, including observability, failure detection, recovery mechanisms, performance monitoring, and appropriate operational controls.

You'll help establish the engineering standards that allow us to safely introduce new models, evaluate changes, manage infrastructure dependencies, and operate increasingly complex AI systems in production.

Reliability can't be something we add after intelligence improves. It has to be built into the systems that deliver it.

Make AI/ML performance measurable

You'll help establish the technical metrics and feedback loops that tell us whether our AI/ML infrastructure is getting better.

That includes measures such as:

Model accuracy and task-level quality
Inference latency and throughput
Cost per inference and cost per successful resolution
Model reliability, availability, and error rates
Evaluation performance and regression detection
Resource utilization and infrastructure efficiency
Time required to evaluate and deploy new model capabilities

You'll work with Product and Engineering to connect these technical improvements to the outcomes that matter most: more accurate decisions, more reliable execution, and greater autonomous resolution.

What We're Looking For

You may be a strong fit if you:

Have 6+ years of relevant software engineering experience, with meaningful ownership of complex technical systems at the Senior or Staff level.
Have built, deployed, or optimized production AI/ML infrastructure, model-serving systems, inference pipelines, or similarly sophisticated AI systems.
Have exceptional engineering fundamentals and strong proficiency in Python, with experience designing and operating reliable distributed systems.
Understand modern foundation models and the tradeoffs involved in model selection, inference architecture, quality, latency, throughput, scalability, and cost.
Have hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure, containerization, orchestration, and the operational challenges of running production AI workloads.
Understand model evaluation and experimentation, and can connect technical changes to measurable improvements in model quality or system performance.
Can move fluidly between foundational architecture, hands-on implementation, performance debugging, and production operations.
Have operated in an environment where technical requirements evolved rapidly and architectural decisions had to balance immediate needs with long-term scalability.
Have strong opinions, loosely held. You can create clarity with incomplete information, explain technical tradeoffs, and adapt quickly as the technology and evidence evolve.
Hold an unusually high bar for engineering quality while still moving with urgency.

Particularly Compelling

We'd be especially interested if you've:

Built foundational AI/ML infrastructure at a breakout AI company or exceptional technology organization where performance, reliability, and scale were critical.
Worked deeply with technologies such as PyTorch, Hugging Face, vLLM, Triton, Ray, Kubernetes, or comparable model-serving and distributed-computing frameworks.
Designed systems for model optimization, fine-tuning, post-training, evaluation, or continuous improvement of production AI capabilities.
Built infrastructure supporting agentic AI systems, complex model orchestration, or multi-step autonomous workflows.
Delivered measurable improvements in model quality, inference efficiency, infrastructure cost, or production reliability.
Built shared technical capabilities from zero, establishing architectures and engineering standards that other teams could build upon.

Experience with supply chain or logistics is useful. However, exceptional engineering judgment, AI/ML systems depth, and a track record of shipping production infrastructure matter more.

This Probably Isn't the Role for You If

Your AI experience is primarily integrating third-party APIs or building lightweight LLM applications without meaningful infrastructure or systems ownership.
Your background is concentrated in theoretical ML research or offline model development, and you haven't owned the engineering required to bring AI capabilities into production.
You're most comfortable operating within an established infrastructure stack rather than defining foundational systems and architectural patterns.
You think optimizing model performance is exclusively about improving benchmark scores, without considering reliability, latency, cost, and real-world outcomes.
You prefer narrowly scoped implementation work over owning difficult technical problems from architecture through production.

Why BackOps

AI has become remarkably good at generating information.

The next frontier is much harder: AI that can be trusted to do the work.

In the physical economy, that means more than producing the right answer. An agent has to understand what's happening, make a decision, interact with real systems, navigate exceptions, communicate with real people, and remain accountable until the problem is actually resolved.

That creates an unusually challenging engineering problem.

You'll help build the AI/ML foundation that makes this possible, determining how models are deployed, evaluated, optimized, and continuously improved as Relay takes on increasingly sophisticated operational work.

Few engineering teams get the opportunity to shape the underlying intelligence and infrastructure of an emerging AI platform while the category itself is still being invented.

That's the opportunity at BackOps.

jobs.description:
About Didi Autonomous Driving

Founded in 2016, DiDi's autonomous driving unit is dedicated to developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology to make transportation safer, more efficient, and accessible. In 2019, the unit became an independent company, Voyager, to accelerate technology development, commercialization, and large-scale deployment. By combining DiDi's unique data advantage, operational expertise, and mobility ecosystem, we aim to build a reliable, scalable autonomous fleet that integrates seamlessly with human-driven services. Driven by real-world customer needs and a strong commitment to safety and user experience
, our mission is to deliver autonomous mobility solutions that create meaningful value for riders and communities.

About The Role

We are looking for an experienced and driven Machine Learning Engineer
to join our autonomous vehicle team and develop the next-generation ML-powered planning system
for Voyager's autonomous driving platform. You will leverage frontier ML techniques, including learned planners and end-to-end models, to build intelligent systems that understand complex driving environments, make data-driven decisions, and navigate safely and efficiently. Working alongside leading industry experts, you will leverage DiDi's unique data advantage
, including petabytes of real-world driving data, to advance model performance, build robust evaluation frameworks that correlate with on-road safety, and accelerate the deployment and scaling of our driverless technology.

Responsibilities

Develop next-generation ML-powered systems that generate driving behavior decisions, scene understanding, and trajectories to support our L4 autonomous driving deployment roadmap.
Frame open-ended, real-world driving challenges as well-defined ML problems; research and apply cutting-edge techniques, including imitation learning, reinforcement learning, learned planners, and end-to-end models.
Design data-driven algorithms that improve the safety, generalization, and reliability of autonomous driving, including robust scene understanding and planning in complex or changing road environments.
Develop hybrid planning solutions that integrate ML-driven approaches with traditional rule-based and optimization-based planning, leveraging their complementary strengths to achieve superior safety, efficiency, and robustness in complex driving scenarios.
Develop and evaluate large-scale ML models using real-world driving data and simulation, translating learned representations into actionable planning guidance and integrating models into production systems under onboard compute, latency, and safety constraints.
Build infrastructure for rapid iteration, including challenging scenario mining, training and evaluation pipelines, closed-loop simulation, and metrics that correlate with real-world driving performance.
Collaborate closely with ML Infrastructure, Perception, Prediction, Planning, Mapping, and Systems Engineering teams to investigate failures, drive end-to-end improvements, and deploy solutions into real-world autonomous driving.

Qualifications

B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
3+ years of industry experience for Senior, or 5+ years for Staff, in machine learning, autonomous driving, robotics, or related fields.
Proven track record of developing and deploying ML models in production, ideally for real-time, embedded, or autonomous driving systems.
Strong proficiency in Python and C++, with experience developing robust, efficient production software and hands-on experience with modern deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow).
Deep understanding of modern deep learning techniques, including transformers, BEV and 3D representations, and trajectory prediction or generation models, with hands-on experience in model training, evaluation, and debugging.
Foundations in linear algebra, control theory, or motion planning, including path and trajectory generation, trajectory evaluation, cost function design, and lane and road geometry.
Experience applying machine learning to motion planning, robotics, or related decision-making problems, with the ability to integrate learning-based approaches with traditional planning methods.
Demonstrated ability to own ambiguous technical challenges end to end, balancing research innovation with production constraints, safety, reliability, and engineering trade-offs.
Demonstrated technical impact through research publications, open-source contributions, or significant achievements in industry.

Preferred Qualifications

Strong engineering experience applying ML-driven approaches to solve complex real-world problems, with a proven track record of translating research ideas into robust, production-quality systems and successfully deploying them.
Experience integrating learning-based approaches with traditional rule-based or optimization-based planning systems to improve safety, efficiency, and robustness.
Experience with closed-loop simulation, large-scale evaluation, and data-driven model iteration for autonomous driving.
Experience mentoring junior engineers, supervising research interns, or leading small technical teams.
Experience with road-structure representations, including lane graphs, topology reasoning, scene understanding, or uncertainty estimation in complex driving environments.
Experience with end-to-end autonomous driving models, learned planners, vision-language models, or foundation models applied to driving and robotics.
Experience deploying and optimizing ML models for real-time onboard inference, including TensorRT, CUDA, quantization, and compute or latency optimization.
Publications at leading conferences such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, or IV, or equivalent demonstrated technical impact in industry.

About The Company

DiDi's autonomous driving unit was established in 2016 with the mission of developing Level 4 autonomous driving (AD) technology to make transportation safer and more efficient. In August 2019, the unit became an independent company, DiDi Autonomous Driving, dedicated to advanced AD R&D, product application, and business expansion. We believe integrating AD technology into a shared-mobility fleet will generate immense social value. By leveraging DiDi's specialized technology, operational expertise, and integrated ecosystem, we are positioned to build and operate a highly efficient, user-oriented autonomous fleet.

About The Role

At DiDi Autonomous Driving, we firmly believe that the future of mobility goes beyond simply "utilizing AI"—it will be fundamentally reimagined and entirely driven by an AI-Native architecture
.

We are seeking a visionary, highly technical, and mission-driven Staff or
Principal AI Transformation Engineer
to act as the ultimate catalyst for our company-wide AI transformation. In this strategic, high-impact leadership role, you will combine cutting-edge Large Language Model (LLM) expertise, robust systems architecture design, and a proven track record of enterprise-level AI scaling. You will embed deeply with our core engineering teams to evolve our traditional R&D organization into a truly AI-Native powerhouse.

Key Responsibilities

AI Infrastructure & Platform Architecture: Spearhead the evaluation, selection, and deep integration of frontier LLM ecosystems (e.g., Llama, Hugging Face) and commercial AI platforms. Own the architectural design of our unified, distributed AI platform spanning complex data processing, model training, inference pipelines, and evaluation frameworks.
Forward Deployed Execution: Embed directly with core autonomous driving teams (Perception, Prediction, Planning & Control, and Simulation) via the FDE model. Pinpoint engineering bottlenecks, eliminate friction, and translate complex AI capabilities into production-ready internal ecosystems (e.g., AI DevOps, AI Copilots).

new_jobs.description:
About BackOps

BackOps is building the AI resolution layer for companies that make or move physical goods.

The physical economy still runs on a fragmented web of ERPs, WMSs, TMSs, carrier and vendor portals, email, spreadsheets, legacy systems, and the people who know how to hold all of it together. When something breaks, whether a shipment is delayed, an order changes, a claim needs to be filed, a document is missing, someone has to gather context across systems, determine what should happen next, take action, and make sure the problem is actually resolved.

BackOps automates that work.

Our platform, Relay, deploys AI operators that understand operational workflows, work across the systems our customers already use, take action, navigate exceptions, and carry work through to resolution. We aren't building another dashboard or copilot. We're building the execution layer that sits between systems and gets the work done.

We recently raised a $42M Series B led by Insight Partners, just six months after our Series A, and are scaling across some of the largest companies in logistics, manufacturing, retail, and other industries that power the physical world.

The opportunity ahead is much larger than any single workflow or vertical. We're building the infrastructure for AI to operate reliably inside the real world.

The Role

As an AI/ML Engineer, you'll own the infrastructure and systems that make Relay's underlying intelligence more capable, efficient, and reliable.

Building an AI operator that can reason through a workflow is one challenge. Making that intelligence perform consistently across thousands of real-world operational scenarios, fragmented enterprise systems, and unpredictable conditions is another.

That's the problem you'll help solve.

You'll work at the intersection of machine learning, distributed systems, and production AI, designing the infrastructure that supports model execution, inference optimization, evaluation, and continuous improvement. You'll help determine how we select, adapt, deploy, and optimize the models powering Relay, balancing intelligence and quality with the performance, scalability, and economics required for enterprise production.

This isn't a role focused on integrating AI APIs or maintaining an established ML stack. You'll make foundational technical decisions, build capabilities from the ground up, and work closely with our CTO and engineering teams to advance the intelligence behind our products.

This is a senior individual contributor role with extraordinary leverage. You'll help define the AI/ML foundation BackOps scales on.

What You'll Own

Build the infrastructure behind Relay's intelligence

Own the architecture and engineering of the AI/ML systems that power Relay, enabling our models to run reliably, efficiently, and at scale.

That may include:

Model serving, inference pipelines, and execution infrastructure
Model selection, routing, and orchestration
Shared interfaces for accessing foundation models and specialized ML capabilities
Infrastructure for experimentation, evaluation, and production deployment
Model versioning, configuration, and lifecycle management
Compute orchestration and resource optimization where appropriate

You'll make pragmatic decisions about what we build, what we leverage from existing providers, and where custom infrastructure creates a meaningful advantage.

Make intelligence faster, more efficient, and more scalable

Our agents need to do more than produce the right answer. They need to operate within the performance and reliability constraints of real enterprise workflows.

You'll optimize the infrastructure and execution patterns that determine how efficiently our models perform, including latency, throughput, scalability, and inference cost.

You'll identify bottlenecks across the AI/ML stack, evaluate architectural tradeoffs, and implement improvements that allow us to support increasingly sophisticated workloads without sacrificing quality or reliability.

The goal isn't simply to make models run faster. It's to make better intelligence economically viable at scale.

Continuously improve model intelligence and quality

Model capability is evolving rapidly. Our ability to translate those advances into better outcomes for customers needs to evolve just as quickly.

You'll develop the systems and technical approaches that allow us to systematically improve model quality and effectiveness.

That may include:

Model evaluation, benchmarking, and comparative testing
Model selection and routing based on task complexity and performance
Context engineering, retrieval, and other techniques that improve model effectiveness
Fine-tuning, model adaptation, or specialized ML approaches where warranted
Experimentation frameworks that connect model changes to measurable improvements in production

You'll partner closely with engineers building Relay's agent capabilities to understand where model limitations create execution failures and determine the most effective way to address them.

Engineer reliability into production AI

AI systems are probabilistic. Enterprise operations demand consistency, accountability, and predictable behavior.

You'll build the infrastructure required to operate AI/ML workloads reliably, including observability, failure detection, recovery mechanisms, performance monitoring, and appropriate operational controls.

You'll help establish the engineering standards that allow us to safely introduce new models, evaluate changes, manage infrastructure dependencies, and operate increasingly complex AI systems in production.

Reliability can't be something we add after intelligence improves. It has to be built into the systems that deliver it.

Make AI/ML performance measurable

You'll help establish the technical metrics and feedback loops that tell us whether our AI/ML infrastructure is getting better.

That includes measures such as:

Model accuracy and task-level quality
Inference latency and throughput
Cost per inference and cost per successful resolution
Model reliability, availability, and error rates
Evaluation performance and regression detection
Resource utilization and infrastructure efficiency
Time required to evaluate and deploy new model capabilities

You'll work with Product and Engineering to connect these technical improvements to the outcomes that matter most: more accurate decisions, more reliable execution, and greater autonomous resolution.

What We're Looking For

You may be a strong fit if you:

Have 6+ years of relevant software engineering experience, with meaningful ownership of complex technical systems at the Senior or Staff level.
